properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-21. Nothing here is intent.

HIS WORDS: "as we are still in development of reflow2, if we add another file, does it automatically get added (being proactive) to a black box or is this something I have to remember (being reactive)? as a user using reflow2 is designing a new project, when do functions get allocated to a black box? again, does reflow2 do this automatically or is it something the user kicks off?" And: "the point on a new project is you don't immediately allocate functions to a black box."

⭐ THIS IS NOT A NEW POSITION — IT IS THE OPEN HALF OF ONE ALREADY ACCEPTED. dec:idea-allocation-waits-for-the-last-responsible-moment settled the PRINCIPLE on 2026-08-14: defer to the last responsible moment, per-capability scope with a project default, and never allocating is a LEGITIMATE TERMINAL STATE rather than a stalled process. What was never settled is WHAT NOTICES THE MOMENT.

⭐⭐ AND THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT RECORDED BESIDE THAT RULING PREDICTED TODAY'S MEASUREMENT, WORD FOR WORD. It was flagged to him before he accepted, and he accepted with it open: "artifacts get written against an assumed structure long before anyone calls allocate. If real files already embody a de facto allocation, then deferring the decision defers only the RECORD of it, and the graph arrives late to something the build already did... it argues the trigger should watch ARTIFACTS APPEARING rather than the allocate call." That was a worry seven days ago. It is now measured.

=== WHAT WAS MEASURED, 2026-08-21, and it is an ASYMMETRY ===

ALLOCATION IS SEMI-AUTOMATIC, and this half works. `unallocated_capability` is a real gap source: capture a capability bound to nothing and it fires on every detect_gaps, appears in loop_status, survives sessions, and the Stop hook nudges when graph writes happen with no loop check. `propose_allocation` will suggest a placement without applying it. So: you capture, reflow2 notices and KEEPS noticing, it can suggest, you decide.

A NEW FILE IS SEEN BY NOTHING. The CI gate builds its observation list by iterating THE ARTIFACTS THE DESIGN ALREADY KNOWS and never walks the disk; reconcile_artifacts does no file I/O at all, so the caller supplies what is looked at. `undocumented_addition` therefore exists as a drift kind THE GATE STRUCTURALLY CANNOT PRODUCE. Add a file, commit, push: every check stays green. The Stop hook does not fire either, because it triggers on GRAPH WRITES and adding a file is not one.

⇒ REFLOW2 IS PROACTIVE ABOUT INTENT IT HOLDS AND BLIND TO REALITY IT DOES NOT. Every automatic mechanism reasons over the graph. The moment the question is "what exists that I was never told about?", nothing looks.

⚠️ AND THE SAME BLIND SPOT WAS JUST FOUND IN THE INSTRUMENT: wall_check walked design-outward-to-files and could not report a file nobody registered, until it was taught to derive its walk roots from the claimed paths. The gate has the identical shape and has not been taught. That the same structural error appeared independently in the tool and the gate is the finding, not the coincidence.

=== OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ===

  (a) THE GATE SWEEPS THE ROOTS THE DESIGN ALREADY POINTS AT and reports files no Artifact claims. Smallest, needs no configuration, and is exactly what wall_check now does — the code exists. Turns 'I forgot' from invisible into a note. ⚠️ Whether it should turn the build RED is a governance question with an owner and must be asked, not assumed.
  (b) MAKE ALLOCATION TIMING RECORDABLE — a date or basis on ALLOCATED_TO. This is the stated TRIGGER of dec:idea-is-allocation-running-ahead-of-the-seams, parked precisely because 156 ALLOCATED_TO edges carry only weight_basis and nothing dates an allocation. Taking it would unpark that question rather than only answering this one.
  (c) A DE FACTO ALLOCATION DETECTOR: when an unclaimed file's neighbours all sit in one component, propose that component. Uses propose_allocation, which already exists and already refuses to apply itself. Strongest reach, and the most likely to propose something confidently wrong — imports are coupling, not intent.
  (d) DO NOTHING; keep it human discipline. The honest option, and the status quo. It is what produced fifteen unmodelled modules and a missed skills_tools over a single day of development.

=== COUNTER-ARGUMENT, BESIDE THE IDEA RATHER THAN AGAINST IT ===

Watching artifacts appear risks re-introducing exactly what the last-responsible-moment ruling was FOR. If every new file prompts 'which black box does this belong to?', the design is pushed back toward allocating early — at the moment of writing a file, which is often earlier than the moment of knowing. The distinction that keeps both: NOTICING a file is unmodelled is not the same as DEMANDING it be allocated. The first is a fact about coverage; the second is a decision about structure. An option that conflates them would undo the ruling while appearing to implement it.

RELATED AND ALREADY SETTLED: dec:idea-allocation-waits-for-the-last-responsible-moment (accepted). PARKED, AND THIS MAY BE ITS TRIGGER: dec:idea-is-allocation-running-ahead-of-the-seams.
properties.name: OPEN — the last responsible moment is agreed, but what WATCHES for it to arrive? Today's measurement says nothing does, and a seven-day-old counter-argument predicted exactly that
